articles.title: Boeing layoffs: Company to cut 5% of commercial airplane workforce as production delays threaten recovery plans
articles.summary: Boeing plans to reduce its commercial airplane division workforce by 5% as it struggles with production delays and misses financial targets.
articles.explain: Boeing is cutting jobs because it cannot produce airplanes as fast as planned, which hurts its bottom line. The company's 'free cash flow' refers to the cash it has available after expenses to invest in its business; missing these targets makes it harder to recover from recent years of turbulence.

story.title: Boeing Workforce and Production Struggles
story.so_far: Boeing has faced significant operational and safety challenges for several years, leading to a long period of regulatory and financial pressure. The company is currently struggling to stabilize its production lines and restore profitability amidst a competitive aerospace market.

articles.title: Yes Bank AT-1 bondholders still await clarity on their money nearly a month after SC verdict
articles.summary: Investors in Yes Bank's AT-1 bonds are still awaiting the restoration of their capital nearly a month after a Supreme Court ruling favored them.
articles.explain: AT-1 bonds are complex, risky financial instruments used by banks to build capital. When Yes Bank was in crisis, regulators canceled these bonds to save the bank. The Supreme Court recently ordered the decision to be overturned, but investors are now struggling with the bureaucratic delay in getting their money back.

story.title: Yes Bank AT-1 Bond Dispute
story.so_far: Yes Bank, a major Indian private lender, underwent a government-led rescue in 2020 to prevent collapse. During that process, AT-1 bonds—a type of high-risk debt instrument—were written down to zero, sparking a years-long legal battle by investors.

timeline.text: Investors in Yes Bank's AT-1 bonds are still awaiting the restoration of their capital nearly a month after a Supreme Court ruling favored them.

articles.title: BNPL makes a comeback as payment apps try to fix its broken economics
articles.summary: Payment apps are attempting to revive the 'Buy Now, Pay Later' (BNPL) model by integrating it with UPI and using repayment behavior to qualify customers for larger loans.
articles.explain: BNPL is a payment option that lets customers pay for goods in installments, often interest-free. Companies are now trying to make it sustainable by linking it to UPI, India's ubiquitous digital payment system, to better track user repayment habits and mitigate the risk of bad debt.

story.title: Evolution of BNPL Payment Models
story.so_far: Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) services surged in popularity as an alternative to credit cards, allowing shoppers to split purchases into installments. However, many early models failed due to high default rates and poor unit economics, leading companies to rethink their strategies.

timeline.text: Payment apps are attempting to revive the 'Buy Now, Pay Later' (BNPL) model by integrating it with UPI and using repayment behavior to qualify customers for larger loans.

articles.title: Pay by the mile! GMR proposes nearly doubling UDF at Bhogapuram airport, drawing IndiGo's ire
articles.summary: GMR Group's proposal to increase airport fees at Bhogapuram has met with resistance from airlines like IndiGo, who warn of increased costs for travelers.
articles.explain: The 'UDF' or User Development Fee is an extra charge added to air tickets to fund airport infrastructure. Airlines argue that doubling this fee will drive up ticket prices, causing travelers to switch to trains for shorter trips and reducing demand for air travel.

story.title: Airport Fee Regulation and Passenger Costs
story.so_far: New airport construction in India, often managed through public-private partnerships (PPP), involves significant upfront costs that developers aim to recover through user fees. These fees are regulated to balance the financial viability of the airport with the affordability of air travel for the public.

articles.title: North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic
articles.summary: North Korean hackers are launching new memecoins to launder funds stolen from a $6.3 billion Binance hack.
articles.explain: A 'memecoin' is a cryptocurrency inspired by internet memes, often lacking traditional utility. In this context, hackers create them as a cover to move money through 'liquidity pools'—decentralized pools of funds—to make it difficult for authorities to track the stolen money back to its source.

story.title: North Korean Crypto Laundering Tactics
story.so_far: North Korean state-sponsored hackers are widely recognized by international intelligence as being responsible for multiple large-scale cryptocurrency exchange breaches. By moving funds through various chains and decentralized protocols, they attempt to bypass global financial sanctions and convert stolen digital assets into usable currency.

timeline.text: Blockchain firm Elliptic discovered hackers using new tokens on the NEAR blockchain to obscure the flow of stolen assets.

articles.title: RBI said to query bank valuations of some bond derivative trades
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is reviewing how banks value certain bond derivative trades, potentially requiring accounting changes.
articles.explain: Bond forwards are contracts to buy or sell bonds at a set price on a future date. 'Level 3' inputs are valuation metrics used when market data is not readily available, making the asset valuation more subjective and requiring higher scrutiny from regulators to ensure accuracy and prevent hidden losses.

story.title: RBI Oversight of Bond Derivatives
story.so_far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) acts as the primary regulator for the nation's banking system. It maintains financial stability by overseeing how banks report their assets, especially complex financial products like derivatives, to ensure they do not pose systemic risk.

timeline.text: The RBI has directed banks to adjust accounting for bond forwards, potentially using 'Level 3' inputs, which could affect asset valuations across the sector.

articles.summary: Oil prices declined following President Trump's remarks aimed at reducing tensions with Iran.
articles.explain: OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is a group of countries that coordinate oil production to influence global prices. A 'blockade' or geopolitical conflict typically pushes prices up due to fears of supply disruption, so news of de-escalation acts as a 'bearish' indicator, lowering prices.

timeline.text: Miners are diversifying into AI infrastructure to offset lower Bitcoin mining revenue and higher operational costs.
